messages.subject: onclick vs onchange
parts:
Hi,

I have a few radio buttons (just as well could have been dropdown list). It is hooked up to Shiny through a reactive function on server side. When the user clicks on a radio button, shiny goes ahead and changes the reactivePrint output as it is hooked up to the reactive input function. 

This all works fine. However what I really want to do is uncheck the radio buttons to have nothing selected between clicks. I am doing that now using onclick javascript on each radio button input.

Now to the issue:

1. User clicks option B
2. shiny reacts and shows the output for option B in reactivePrint
3. js resets radio to have nothing checked. Now no option is selected.
4. User clicks option B again, nothing happens.
5. User clicks any other option (say option A), now shiny reacts and shows the output for option A in reactivePrint

The problem is that user has to click a different value the next time for this to work. They cannot click the same value. This is probably because shiny is looking for changes in the radio button. And since the value now is the same as before, it thinks there is no change. 

In other words, I want to reset the value of the input between displays of output. 

Thanks

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: onclick vs onchange
parts:
Sorry for the delay in responding. When step 3 happens, would you like the Shiny app to be notified that nothing is selected? If so, you need to use jQuery to trigger a "change" event on the radio in question.

$(radioEl).trigger("change")

I haven't tried it but this seems like it should work.

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: onclick vs onchange
parts:
Can you elaborate why this is required? I encountered the same problem while using jQuery to directly reset a shiny action button. I had to click the action button twice to activate the required action. I solved the issue in a similar fashion by adding a $(actionEl).click()  after the jQuery action.

I believe understanding this would be important for users who will be using jQuery and Shiny in tandem, as it makes things a lot easier.
